# TDPdf v1.30.1.0

**The printer's own Properties dialog now actually does something.** Everything you set there was being collected and thrown away.

## Fixed

### Printer Properties settings were discarded

Click **Properties…** in the print window and you get your printer's own driver dialog — the real one, with the vendor's tabs. You set your paper, your finishing, your quality, you press OK, and the dialog closes.

TDPdf then freed the driver's answer without reading a byte of it, and built the job from a fresh ticket that knew only about the dozen options in TDPdf's own sidebar. Every choice made in that dialog was collected and dropped, every time. The dialog worked; nothing it did survived the OK button.

The driver's result is now converted into the print ticket the job is actually built from. That covers the settings Windows has standard names for, and — more to the point — the ones it doesn't: **folding, hole punch, output bin, secure print PINs, toner save, the vendor's own quality panels.** Those live only inside the driver's private data, which is exactly what was being discarded.

Three smaller things came with it:

- **The dialog opens showing this job's settings** — the paper, orientation and two-sided choice currently set in TDPdf — rather than the printer's stored defaults.
- **What you change there is read back into the sidebar**, so the two can never disagree in silence. Set landscape in the driver dialog and TDPdf's Orientation now says landscape, and the preview redraws to match.
- **Cancel means cancel.** It previously made no difference either way, since nothing was applied; now it leaves both the job and the sidebar untouched.

### The preview could show the wrong paper

A paper size chosen in the driver dialog didn't reach the preview, so the sheet on screen could be a different stock from the one the job printed on. The preview is now sized from the same ticket the job uses.

### "Pages per sheet" in the driver dialog printed four to a side

TDPdf composes the tiled sheet itself. A driver that had also been asked to tile was tiling the already-tiled sheet, so asking for two pages per side in the driver dialog produced four. That choice is now taken up by TDPdf's own **Pages per sheet** control — where the preview can show it — and applied once.

## Note on folding

Folding, hole punch and output bin have no portable name in the Windows print schema — they exist only in each driver's own dialog, under each vendor's own naming. TDPdf can't offer them as its own controls without guessing per-driver keywords and getting it wrong on half the fleet.

What it can do, and now does, is carry them through faithfully: set them in **Properties…** and they reach the job. The print window points at that dialog so it's clear where they live.

## Installing

Managed machines update through Intune automatically; nothing to do. Otherwise it's the same self-contained `TDPdf.exe`.
